models_evaluated: Google investigational mammography AI triage device

links.outcome: Time to additional imaging and biopsy diagnosis with AI prioritization vs standard
links.effect: Mean time to additional imaging fell 25% (25.6 to 19.1 days, p<0.001); time to biopsy fell 30% (55.9 to 39.2 days, p=0.003); all 6 cancers AI-prioritized.
links.quote: In comparison, mean T A in the experimental group was reduced by 25% to 19.1 days (ΔT A =−6.4 days, upper limit of one-sided 95% CI = −0.3, p <0.001), while the mean T B was reduced by 30% to 39.2 days (ΔT B =−16.8 days, upper limit of one-sided 95% CI = −5.1, p =0.003).

links.outcome: Real-world prioritization rate vs retrospective expectation
links.effect: AI prioritized 29% of cases in deployment vs 14% anticipated from retrospective testing, requiring more immediate reads than planned.
links.quote: First, the proportion of cases prioritized by AI for immediate radiologist review was 29%, much higher than the proportion anticipated based on retrospective testing (14%).

links.outcome: Radiologist recall rate and influence of AI prioritization on interpretation
links.effect: Recall 17.0% experimental vs 14.3% control (p=0.36, not significant); radiologists reported discomfort calling AI-prioritized cases normal, especially initially.
links.quote: This difference was not statistically significant ( p =0.36).

models_evaluated: Investigational mammography AI prioritization device based on McKinney et al. (2020)

links.outcome: Time to additional imaging and biopsy diagnosis
links.effect: Mean time to additional imaging: 25.6 to 19.1 days (25% reduction; p <0.001). Mean time to biopsy diagnosis: 55.9 to 39.2 days (30% reduction; p =0.003).
links.quote: In comparison, mean T A in the experimental group was reduced by 25% to 19.1 days (ΔT A =−6.4 days, upper limit of one-sided 95% CI = −0.3, p <0.001), while the mean T B was reduced by 30% to 39.2 days (ΔT B =−16.8 days, upper limit of one-sided 95% CI = −5.1, p =0.003).

links.outcome: Prospective versus retrospectively anticipated AI prioritization rate
links.effect: AI prioritized 29% of cases for immediate radiologist review, compared with 14% anticipated from retrospective testing, requiring more immediate interpretations than expected.
links.quote: First, the proportion of cases prioritized by AI for immediate radiologist review was 29%, much higher than the proportion anticipated based on retrospective testing (14%).

links.outcome: Staff capacity to provide immediate interpretation and same-visit diagnostic imaging
links.effect: Radiologists were unavailable within 30 minutes for 6% (8/131) of prioritized cases; 15% (5/33) needing additional imaging were not offered same-visit imaging for operational reasons.
links.quote: For 6% (8/131) of AI-prioritized cases, a radiologist was not available to perform an interpretation within 30 minutes; these participants obtained their final screening results by letter as usual (all had negative or benign findings).

links.outcome: Failures of AI integration with site software
links.effect: AI integration with site software failed in 3 cases due to a software error.
links.quote: In 3 cases AI integration with site software failed due to a software error.
